meta.title: GDP Doesn't Count Half Of What Actually Keeps America Running
meta.hook: In 2025 the US economy was measured at over thirty trillion dollars. Huge parts of it were never counted.
meta.description: GDP totals the market value of all goods and services a country produces in a year — in 2025 that figure for the US was measured at over $30 trillion by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. But GDP only counts what's bought and sold. Unpaid childcare, informal caregiving, and household work never show up in the number, even though they're real economic activity. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: In twenty twenty-five, the US economy was measured at over thirty trillion dollars. And that number leaves things out.

visual.query: large glowing number thirty trillion screen
visual.visual_intent: A massive glowing dollar figure on a dark data screen, camera pushing in, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: hook: BEA 2025 nominal GDP figure, cited with year attribution

scenes.narration: That number is GDP. Gross Domestic Product. It totals the market value of everything bought and sold in a year.

visual.query: goods and services icons flowing screen
visual.visual_intent: Simple icons of goods and services flowing across a dark screen into a single total, clean motion graphic
visual.decision_reason: the formal definition, BEA's own framing

scenes.narration: But 'bought and sold' is the key phrase. If money doesn't change hands for it, GDP doesn't see it.

visual.visual_intent: A hand writing that fades to invisible on a page, symbolic of unseen activity, cinematic

scenes.narration: A parent caring for their own kids at home. A neighbor doing unpaid caregiving. Real work. Zero dollars in GDP.

visual.query: parent caring for child home warm light
visual.visual_intent: A parent gently caring for a child at home, warm natural light, tender documentary realism
visual.decision_reason: the concrete example of excluded activity

scenes.narration: Economists have debated this gap for decades. It's not a flaw exactly, it's just what the number was built to measure.

visual.query: economist looking at data charts office
visual.visual_intent: A person reviewing printed economic charts at a desk, thoughtful, natural office light, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: acknowledges the well-known economist critique without inventing a specific study or number

scenes.narration: GDP tells you the size of the market economy. It was never built to tell you the whole economy. Follow for more.

visual.visual_intent: A simple scale on a dark background, one side lit and one side dim, symbolic composition
